This clause describes the Admiralty jurisdiction of the Supreme Court "as the same is used and exercised in that part of Great Britain called 'England' together with all and singular incidents, emergent and dependencies annexed". The jurisdiction was continued by Clause 31 of the Letters Patent of 1862 and clause 32 of the Letters Patent of 1865. 

 9. In order to bring about uniformity between the jurisdiction of the High Court of Admiralty in England and the Admiralty Jurisdiction of High Courts in British possessions the British Parliament enacted the Colonial Courts of Admiralty Act, 1890. Pursuant to that Act the Colonial Courts of Admiralty Act (India) 1891 was passed declaring certain courts including the High Courts of Judicature at Fort William in Bengal as the Colonial Courts of Admiralty so that they could exercise the same jurisdiction as that of the High Court of England, as existing in 1890 by virtue of any statute or otherwise". In 1890 the Admiralty jurisdiction of t he High Court of England was used to be exercised under the Admiralty Act of 1861 of the British Parliament which became the basis of the Admiralty jurisdiction of the High Court of Calcutta. The Admiralty rules framed by the High Court of Calcutta came into operation in June, 1912 the jurisdiction was preserved by section 106 of the Government of India Act, 1915 and section 223 of the Government of India Act, 1935. In 1947 in exercise of the power conferred by section 9 of the Indian Independence Act, 1947, the High Courts (Bengal) Order, 1947 was passed. Paragraph 5 of the Order provided: 

 10. So far as the present action for non-delivery of the Plaintiff's cargo is concerned the jurisdiction of this Court is not derived from the Letters Patent of 1862 or that of 1865, but from the Colonial Courts of Admiralty Act (India) of 1891 and the Court of Admiralty Act, 1861 of England. The latter Act is not on our statute book but it is administered in view of the combined operation of sub-section (2) of section 2 of the colonial Courts of Admiralty Act 1890 of the British Parliament and the Colonial Courts of Admiralty Act (India) 1891, the latter Act being revised by the Bangladesh Laws (Revision and Declaration) Act, 1973 (Act VIII of 1973) is now on our statute book. It is true that if the revised Court of Admiralty Act of 1891 is read in isolation then it would not give any idea as to the nature and extent of the Admiralty jurisdiction of this Court, but it is to be read in its historical perspective. Under the Act of 1891 the High Court Division of this Court was declared as the Court of Admiralty. This Court exercises the, same jurisdiction as the High Court of England exercised in 1890 under the Admiralty Court Act of 1861. 

 11. Under section 6 of the Admiralty Court Act, 1861 the High Court of England had jurisdiction to hear and determine any claim relating to carriage of goods in a ship. The instant suit arising out of a claim for non-delivery or the cargo that was to be carried by the ship Nedlloyd Leave is amenable to the jurisdiction of this Court. In view of the above, Issue No.1 is decided in favour of the plaintiff.
